summary: Today’s pulse tracks Supreme’s court decision seems to spell end for Republican-drawn congressional maps in Missouri – US politics live, Trump promise of $5,000 for US citizens after midterms decried as ‘bribery’, and US supreme court again rejects Missouri maps drawn to boost Republicans in midterms. Across Guardian and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are trump, court, and midterm. In the background, Four people in hospital after reports of stabbing in south-east London and TV presenter v secret son: the succession dispute engulfing a Ugandan kingdom keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Supreme’s court decision seems to spell end for Republican-drawn congressional maps in Missouri – US politics live
headlines.description: Court’s decision to block federal judge’s ruling likely to prevent GOP’s attempts to extract additional Republican-leaning seat US supreme court again rejects Missouri congressional maps redrawn to benefit Republicans in midterms The decision, issued by Justice Brett Kavanaugh, appeared to sound a death knell for efforts by the Missouri GOP to extract an additional Republican-leaning congressional seat for their party ahead of the midterm elections.

headlines.title: Trump promise of $5,000 for US citizens after midterms decried as ‘bribery’
headlines.description: Critics react to bid for Republican votes with incredulity and point to potential $1.2tn cost atop existing national debt Donald Trump’s promise of a $5,000 “Trump dividend” for every US citizen if Republicans retain control of the US Congress in November’s midterm elections has sparked incredulity and accusations of bribery. “If the Republicans win, you win with us and you get $5,000,” Trump said during the unprecedented Republican midterm convention in Dallas. “It will be called the Trump dividend.”

headlines.title: US supreme court again rejects Missouri maps drawn to boost Republicans in midterms
headlines.description: Latest decision appears to set the stage for the state to use its old electoral maps this year The US supreme court again rejected a push backed by Donald Trump to overhaul Missouri’s congressional maps in an effort to hand Republicans an edge in November’s midterm elections. Its latest ruling, after days of confusion , comes less than two months before the pivotal midterm elections in which control of the narrowly divided US House of Representatives could be determined by a handful of seats.

headlines.title: Four people in hospital after reports of stabbing in south-east London
headlines.description: Emergency services dispatched to scene on Bromley High Street on Thursday afternoon Four people have been taken to hospital after reports of a stabbing in south-east London, emergency services said. London ambulance service was called to reports of a stabbing on Bromley High Street at 2.19pm on Thursday.

headlines.title: TV presenter v secret son: the succession dispute engulfing a Ugandan kingdom
headlines.description: Family of late King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV reveal son’s existence as they reject committee’s choice of cousin as new monarch A traditional Ugandan kingdom has become engulfed in a bitter succession dispute after the family of a king who recently died rejected the selection of a television news anchor as his successor. King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch when he took the throne in the kingdom of Tooro in 1995 at the age of three, died on 27 August in the US, where he was receiving cancer treatment.

headlines.title: Barbara Keating died in the 9/11 attack. She's finally being laid to rest
headlines.description: Barbara Keating died aboard one of the planes that hijackers slammed into the World Trade Center. Her remains were finally identified last year, and her family is gathering for a long-delayed funeral.

headlinePool.title: UK politics: Visitor levy powers should be in place by March 2028 in England, ministers say – as it happened
headlinePool.description: Downing Street gives more details of plan, saying it would be charged as a percentage of accommodation costs, not a flat fee Tourists in England face nightly levy on hotel and Airbnb stays under new plans The Centre for Cities , a thinktank that focuses on promoting growth in cities, has welcomed the government’s plans to let mayors in England impose a tourism tax. This is from its chief executive, Andrew Carter. The overnight visitor levy is a great step forward for fiscal devolution. This marks the first time that mayors in England have gained more autonomy over funding. The overnight visitor levy means places will get rewarded for doing what they need to attract more visitors and grow their local economies. Labour’s solution to every issue is always to hike taxes. This is just the latest method they’ve found to squeeze more money out of hardworking families and the economy. The hospitality industry has already been hit by colossal business rates hikes thanks to Labour, on top of their Jobs Tax and employment red tape that have driven up costs. Now hotels and other businesses face another blow that will harm local economies and discourage local tourism. VAT is already charged at 20% on hotels - much higher than in other countries - and now they’ll pay VAT on this tourism tax too: a Labour double whammy.

headlinePool.title: MPs on both sides urge Commons not to take ‘extraordinary risk’ of forcing through assisted dying bill
headlinePool.description: Labour MPs Gareth Snell and Meg Hillier say Lords must be allowed to fulfil duty in scrutinising bill on serious public issue UK politics live – latest updates MPs who voted for and against assisted dying have urged their respective sides not to take the “extraordinary risk” of forcing through the bill using an obscure parliamentary procedure if it continues to be blocked by the Lords. Two Labour MPs have written a warning letter to colleagues in the crucial hours before the next vote on Friday: Gareth Snell, who voted in favour of the bill, and Meg Hillier, who voted against.

headlinePool.title: Orthodox church sends medieval prince’s remains to Russian troops in Ukraine
headlinePool.description: Part of Dmitry Donskoy’s right hand sent to ‘spiritually strengthen’ soldiers The Russian Orthodox church has sent a fragment of a medieval warrior prince’s remains to troops fighting in Ukraine, saying the relic would “spiritually strengthen” soldiers and help them achieve victory. A reliquary containing part of the right hand of Dmitry Donskoy, the 14th-century prince revered in Russia for his victory over the Mongolian Golden Horde in 1380, has been taken to Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and is now being transported along the frontline.

headlinePool.title: Russia’s actions have strengthened European case for boosting defence spending, says Nato chief – as it happened
headlinePool.description: Mark Rutte said that Europeans ‘increasingly understand’ the need for their countries to take ‘greater responsibility for our own security’ Addressing German ambassadors, Wadephul repeats that the Russian threat “has reached our doorstep and it’s tangible.” He adds: “The Russian attempted attack at the airport in Leipzig is only the most recent incident in a string of constantly growing Russian aggression against Europe and against Nato. Russia and its partners operate with a global network against our interests and in favour of an own imperialist claim to great power status."

headlinePool.title: 'I've never seen anything like this' -- A U.S. doctor treats Ebola's youngest victims
headlinePool.description: Dr. Rupa Narra is a U.S. pediatrician who arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo to help care for stricken children. Nothing could have prepared her for what she'd face.

headlinePool.title: ‘I don’t want to be here’: Andrew Hastie was a reluctant but ‘straightforward’ witness in the Ben Roberts-Smith defamation case
headlinePool.description: The Liberal MP and former SAS soldier is under attack from One Nation after complying with a subpoena to give evidence in the failed 2022 civil case I pity Mr Roberts-Smith. I pity this whole process. I don’t want to be here.” Andrew Hastie was a reluctant witness in the Ben Roberts-Smith defamation case. Hastie appeared only under force of subpoena in 2022: compelled to attend court, obliged to swear an oath, and to tell “the whole truth and nothing but the truth”. headlinePool.title: Woolworths increased prices of at least four ‘family staples’ during ‘Price Freeze’ promotion
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: Analysis shows cost of chicken fillets, potatoes and donuts rose during supermarket giant’s three-month promotion Pricing data, compiled by comparison website CW Scanner and provided to Guardian Australia, shows the supermarket chain increasing the prices of at least four key products after starting the three-month “Price Freeze” promotion on 1 May.

headlinePool.title: How did 9/11 reshape national security?
headlinePool.description: Sept. 11 represented a new kind of national security threat, and a new national security architecture was created to confront it.

headlinePool.title: Florida man scheduled for execution in connection to Hog Trail Murders
headlinePool.description: Daniel Owen Conahan Jr’s sentence will make him the state’s 15th person executed this year A Florida man was scheduled for execution on Thursday after being convicted of one of a series of suspected killings that became known as the Hog Trail Murders in the 1990s. Daniel Owen Conahan Jr, 72, was sentenced to die by lethal injection for the 1996 kidnapping and strangling of Richard Allen Montgomery. Authorities found Montgomery’s mutilated body in a wooded south-west Florida area where the remains of at least six people have been found over a three-year span.
